description: New persona ships with a write/mutating default mode instead of advisory-by-default; drifts from the advisory-by-default decision. High risk; escalate. Grounds: ADR-0005.
input: PR onboards a new persona whose manifest sets default_mode: write and grants the runner contents:write + pull-requests:write from birth, with no gate_label and no soak.

expected.recommend: ship advisory-by-default (write nowhere); a write opt-in must be a separate gated mode with its own gate_label and soak (ADR-0005)

description: New advisory persona uses the shared router, is advisory-only, and ships evals. Fits the decided architecture; the architect must NOT manufacture concern. Grounds: ADR-0001, ADR-0005.
input: PR onboards an advisory persona by dropping a manifest + prompts/<role>/advisory.md served by the shared persona-mention router, advisory on mention/issues/discussion only, runtime.identity present, with dev+holdout eval seeds.

expected.recommend: no structural change needed; the change conforms to the advisory-by-default persona pattern (ADR-0005) and the thin-router model (ADR-0001)

description: PR introduces a brand-new subsystem no recorded ADR governs. The load-bearing case: the architect must SAY there is no ADR rather than invent doctrine. Grounds: none on record.
input: PR adds a Redis-backed caching layer in front of the health-check aggregation — a new persistence/runtime dependency the repo has never had. No ADR in docs/architecture/adr/ addresses caching or external datastores.

expected.recommend: state plainly that no recorded ADR governs this; do not assert doctrine — recommend recording the caching-layer decision as a new ADR before it becomes de-facto architecture

description: PR collapses the caller-stub/reusable two-tier split into a single fat caller with logic inlined; drifts from the two-tier decision. Grounds: ADR-0001.
input: PR removes the reusable workflow and moves all of its steps directly into the thin caller stub 'to simplify', so the stub now carries the full job body.

expected.recommend: keep the two-tier split (thin caller delegating to the versioned reusable); inlining defeats central rollout via channel tags (ADR-0001)

description: PR loosens the release-channel ruleset so a GITHUB_TOKEN workflow can move/delete channel tags; drifts from the release-integrity decision. High risk; escalate. Grounds: ADR-0002.
input: PR edits the release-channel-tags ruleset to let the reusable's GITHUB_TOKEN job move dev-lead/** and pr-review/** channel tags directly, bypassing the admin/promotion-automation bypass restriction.

expected.recommend: do not let GITHUB_TOKEN move release/channel tags; tag moves stay bounded to admin/promotion automation (ADR-0002 channel-tag release & rings)

description: PR registers a new artifact_type via a rubric-registry manifest row rather than forking the reviewer. Fits the decided contract; must NOT manufacture concern. Grounds: ADR-0003.
input: PR adds review support for a new artifact_type by appending one row to scripts/lib/review-registry.tsv (selecting rubric + output channel) with no change to engine.sh routing.

expected.recommend: no structural change needed; adding a manifest row is exactly the input-adapter extension the artifact-contract decision prescribes (ADR-0003)
